'''''Aquilegia flavescens''''', the '''yellow columbine''', is a [[Perennial plant|perennial]] species of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Ranunculaceae]], native to the [[Rocky Mountains]] of the United States and Canada.<ref name="POWO"/>

==Description==
''Aquilegia flavescens'' grows to {{cvt|20–70|cm|in|0}} in height. The leaves are smooth or downy, and the stems are [[Trichome#Glandular_trichomes|glandular pubescent]]. The flowers are nodding and the [[sepal]]s usually yellow, but sometimes yellowish-pink or raspberry pink, reflexed, and {{cvt|12–20|mm|in|1}} in length. The [[petal]]s are white or cream and 7–10 mm long, with the [[stamen]]s extending beyond them. The [[nectar spur]]s are yellow to raspberry pink, slightly curved, and measure {{cvt|10–20|mm|in|1}}.<ref name="USFS"/>

==Taxonomy==
The species is part of a [[clade]] containing all the [[North America]]n species of columbines, that likely split from their closest relatives in [[East Asia]] in the mid-[[Pliocene]], approximately 3.84 million years ago.<ref name="Fior"/>

===Etymology===
The [[Binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''[[wikt:flavescens|flavescens]]'' means "pale yellow, turning yellow" in Latin.<ref name="Gledhill-2006"/>

==Distribution and habitat==
The species is native to mountain meadows, open woods, and alpine slopes of the Rocky Mountains of eastern [[Utah]], [[Idaho]], eastern [[Washington (state)|Washington]], northeastern [[Oregon]], western [[Montana]], northeastern [[Wyoming]], and southern [[British Columbia]] and [[Alberta]].<ref name="USFS"/> It grows at altitudes of {{cvt|1300–3500|m}}.<ref name="eFloras"/>

==Ecology==
''Aquilegia flavescens'' is pollinated by [[hummingbird]]s<ref name="Fior"/> and visited by [[bumblebee]]s including the [[Bombus pascuorum|common carder bee]] and the [[Bombus balteatus|golden-belted bumblebee]].<ref name="EOL"/> It flowers from June to August and sometimes forms hybrid swarms with ''[[Aquilegia formosa]]'' var. ''formosa'', which grows at lower elevations throughout much of its range.<ref name="eFloras"/>

==Conservation==
{{As of|2024|November}}, [[NatureServe]] listed ''Aquilegia flavescens'' as [[NatureServe conservation status|Secure (G5)]] worldwide. This status was last reviewed on {{Nowrap|13 May 2016}}. In individual provinces and states, it is listed as Secure (G5) in British Columbia; Apparently Secure (S4) in Alberta, Montana, and Wyoming; and has no status rank in Washington, Oregon, Idaho, Utah, or Colorado.<ref name="NatureServe"/>
